title: Mutation Behind a Shared Reference
goal: Cell and RefCell move the mutability check inside the value.

sections.text: Normally, mutation requires exclusive access: a `&self` method cannot assign to its fields, error `E0594`. Interior mutability moves the permission inside the value: the field itself allows controlled mutation through a shared reference. This is how a counter can live behind `&self`, or how shared `Rc` handles can still update the value they share.

sections.caption: Cell copies values in and out. No guards, no panics.

sections.text: `Cell<T>` is the simple form, for `Copy` types like `u32`. `get()` copies the value out, `set()` replaces it. Nothing can go wrong at runtime. `RefCell<T>` handles non-Copy types like `Vec`: `borrow()` gives a read guard, `borrow_mut()` gives a write guard, and the borrow rules are enforced at runtime instead of compile time.

Runtime enforcement means a new failure mode: holding a read guard in a variable while asking for a write guard panics with already borrowed. Keep guards as short-lived as the syntax allows, and prefer the one-statement form `cell.borrow().len()` that releases the guard immediately.

explanation: Cell for Copy types, RefCell for the rest. RefCell checks the borrow rules at runtime, so keep its guards short.
